dialogue.origin: (こんにちは本日は宜しくお願いいたします)
dialogue.content: (Hello. Thank you for coming in today. I look forward to our session.)

dialogue.origin: （よろしくお願いします）
dialogue.content: (Thank you. I look forward to it as well.)

dialogue.origin: (時間になりましたら始めさせていただきますね)
dialogue.content: (We'll begin when it's time.)

dialogue.origin: こんにちは、相談員です今日はご相談ありがとうございますまずはじめに年齢、性別をお聞かせいただけますか？
dialogue.content: Hello, I'm the counselor. Thank you for coming in for a consultation today. First, could you please tell me your age and gender?

dialogue.origin: こんにちは。22歳女性です。
dialogue.content: Hello. I'm a 22-year-old woman.

dialogue.origin: ありがとうございます本日はどのようなご相談でしょうか？
dialogue.content: Thank you. What would you like to discuss today?

dialogue.origin: 就活がうまくいかなくて悩んでいます。
dialogue.content: I'm struggling with my job hunting.

dialogue.origin: なるほど、就活のお悩みですね
dialogue.content: I see, so you're concerned about your job search.

dialogue.origin: はい、そうなんです
dialogue.content: Yes, that's right.

dialogue.origin: 就活のお悩みというと具体的にはどういったことに悩んでおられますでしょうか？
dialogue.content: When you say you're concerned about your job search, what specifically are you worried about?

dialogue.origin: 冬くらいから就活をしているのですが、なかなか決まらなくて焦っています
dialogue.content: I've been job hunting since around winter, but nothing has worked out, and I'm starting to feel anxious.

dialogue.origin: そうだったんですね、なかなか決まらないと不安になってきますよね
dialogue.content: I understand. It's natural to feel anxious when you can't seem to find a job, isn't it?

dialogue.origin: はい。不安ですね
dialogue.content: Yes. I'm feeling anxious.

dialogue.origin: ちなみに今は学生さんでしょうか？それとも何かお仕事されていらっしゃいますか？
dialogue.content: By the way, are you currently a student, or are you working?

dialogue.origin: 今は大学4年生です
dialogue.content: I'm currently a fourth-year university student.

dialogue.origin: なるほど、新卒で就活中ということですね
dialogue.content: I see, so you're job hunting as a soon-to-be graduate.

dialogue.origin: そうなんです
dialogue.content: That's right.

dialogue.origin: では大変な時期ですよね現在はどのような分野がご希望でエントリーされていらっしゃいますか？
dialogue.content: This must be a challenging time. What fields are you hoping for and currently applying to?

dialogue.origin: 今は事務職を探しています。でもどこも倍率が高くて受かりません
dialogue.content: I'm looking for administrative positions right now. But the competition is high everywhere, and I can't seem to get accepted.

dialogue.origin: なるほど、競争相手が多くて難しいのですね
dialogue.content: I understand, it's tough with so many competitors.

dialogue.origin: 今までに何社くらい受けられたのでしょうか？
dialogue.content: About how many companies have you applied to so far?

dialogue.origin: 50社以上は受けたと思います。
dialogue.content: I think I've applied to over 50 companies.

dialogue.origin: そうだったんですね50社以上とはそれはたくさん受けられているのですねとても頑張ってこれたのですね
dialogue.content: I see. More than 50—that's a lot of companies. You've been working very hard, haven't you?

dialogue.origin: はい。沢山受けたんですけど全部落ちちゃって、、辛いです
dialogue.content: Yes. I've applied to so many, but I've been rejected by all of them... It's really tough.

dialogue.origin: そうですよね、たくさん行動しておられたからこそやはり辛し、悲しいお気持ちになりますよね
dialogue.content: I can understand that. Precisely because you've put in so much effort, it must feel very painful and sad.

dialogue.origin: はい。周りもどんどん決まってきてるし焦りもあります
dialogue.content: Yes. My peers are getting offers one after another, and it makes me feel even more anxious.

dialogue.origin: ええ、周りの方が決まっていくと焦ってしまいますよね。就職活動の中で特にどのような事が一番大変だとお感じになられますか？
dialogue.content: Yes, it's natural to feel anxious when you see others securing jobs. During your job search, what do you find to be the most difficult part?

dialogue.origin: まず、面接が苦手なんです。
dialogue.content: First of all, I'm not good at interviews.

dialogue.origin: なるほど、面接が大変なんですね面接のどういったところが苦手と感じておられますか？
dialogue.content: I see, interviews are difficult for you. What aspects of interviews do you find challenging?

dialogue.origin: 人前で話すのが苦手で、、緊張しちゃうんです。集団面接とかだと全然うまく話せません
dialogue.content: I'm not good at speaking in front of people... I get really nervous. In group interviews, for example, I can't speak well at all.

dialogue.origin: そうでしたか、人前で話すのって緊張しますよねそれはとてもしんどいですよね
dialogue.content: I see. Speaking in front of people can be nerve-wracking, can't it? That must be very tough.

dialogue.origin: はい。だから面接までいってもうまく話せなくて落ちちゃうんですよね
dialogue.content: Yes. That's why even when I make it to the interview, I can't speak well and end up getting rejected.

dialogue.origin: なるほど、面接でうまく話せないのが原因だとお考えになっておられるのですね
dialogue.content: I see, so you feel that not being able to speak well in interviews is the main reason.

dialogue.origin: 面接は初めて会う方ばかりだとおもいますが、
dialogue.content: I imagine that in interviews, you're always meeting people for the first time,

dialogue.origin: 普段知っている人と話すのはどうですか？
dialogue.content: but how is it when you talk to people you know?

dialogue.origin: それは問題なく話せます。
dialogue.content: I can talk with them without any problem.

dialogue.origin: そうなのですね面接で上手く話せないとおっしゃっていましたが、どういう場面が上手くいかないと感じておられますか？
dialogue.content: I see. You mentioned that you find it hard to speak well in interviews—in what kinds of situations do you feel things don't go well?

dialogue.origin: いっぱい聞かれそうな質問の答えを準備して行っても、予想外のことを聞かれると頭が真っ白になっちゃって
dialogue.content: Even if I prepare answers for all the likely questions, when I'm asked something unexpected, my mind goes completely blank.

dialogue.origin: ええ、準備していなかった質問がくると頭が真っ白になって上手くいかないということなんですね予想外のことには慌ててしまいますよね
dialogue.content: Yes, so when you get a question you haven't prepared for, your mind goes blank and it doesn't go well. It's natural to be flustered by the unexpected, isn't it?

dialogue.origin: はい。あと面接官が2.3人いたりとかすると物凄く緊張します
dialogue.content: Yes. Also, I get extremely nervous when there are two or three interviewers.

dialogue.origin: そうなんですね、しらない年上の方が複数人いるという環境は緊張しても自然な状況ですよね。
dialogue.content: I see. It's quite natural to feel nervous in an environment with multiple older people you don't know, isn't it?

dialogue.origin: では、今までのお話をまとめさせていただきますと、
dialogue.content: Okay, let me summarize what you've shared with me so far:

dialogue.origin: 冬から就職活動を続けておられる状況で、現状ではまだ内定をもらっていない状態でまわりが決まっているのをみると焦って不安になっておられる、
dialogue.content: You've been job hunting since winter and still haven't received an offer. Seeing others around you getting jobs is making you feel anxious and worried,

dialogue.origin: 就活の中では面接がとても緊張して準備をしっかりしていても予想外の質問だあったり、面接官が複数いたりするとさらに緊張して頭が真っ白になって困っているといった状況ですね
dialogue.content: and within your job search, you find interviews very nerve-wracking. Even with thorough preparation, unexpected questions or the presence of multiple interviewers makes you even more nervous, causing your mind to go blank and leaving you feeling stuck. Is that about right?

dialogue.origin: はい、そんな感じです
dialogue.content: Yes, that's about right.

dialogue.origin: ありがとうございますでは今日は今感じておられる焦りや不安を少しでも解消できればいいなということでのご相談ということで合っていますでしょうか？
dialogue.content: Thank you. So, is it correct to say that your goal for today's session is to find a way to alleviate the anxiety and worry you're feeling, even just a little?

dialogue.origin: そうですね。あとどうやったら緊張せずに面接を受けられるか知りたいです
dialogue.content: That's right. I'd also like to know how I can go into interviews without getting so nervous.

dialogue.origin: ええ、緊張せずに面接を受けられると嬉しいですよね
dialogue.content: Yes, it would be great if you could get through interviews without feeling so nervous, wouldn't it?

dialogue.origin: はい。そうしたら内定もらえる気がします
dialogue.content: Yes. I feel like I could get an offer if I were able to do that.

dialogue.origin: はい、内定が早くもらえるといいですよね
dialogue.content: Yes, it would be great to get an offer soon, wouldn't it?

dialogue.origin: 相談員さんは緊張しますか？
dialogue.content: Do you get nervous, counselor?

dialogue.origin: そうですね、私もやはり初めての場所や初めて会う人と話す時はとても緊張します
dialogue.content: That's a good question. Yes, I also get very nervous in new places or when talking to people I'm meeting for the first time.

dialogue.origin: 手が震えたりすることもあります
dialogue.content: Sometimes my hands even shake.

dialogue.origin: ですよね。どうやったら緊張せずに面接受けられるんでしょうか
dialogue.content: Right? So how can I get through an interview without being nervous?

dialogue.origin: はい、一緒に考えさせていただいますね
dialogue.content: Yes, let's think about that together.

dialogue.origin: 面接も嫌になります
dialogue.content: I'm starting to hate interviews.

dialogue.origin: そうですよね、面接が嫌になると今まで頑張ってこられたのに、もったいないですしね
dialogue.content: I can understand that. It would be a shame to start hating interviews after all the hard work you've put in, wouldn't it?

dialogue.origin: 面接で緊張するときに何か試してみた事などはおありですか？
dialogue.content: Have you tried anything to manage your nervousness during interviews?

dialogue.origin: 頭が真っ白にならないように準備だけはしておこうと思っていっぱい練習はしているんですけど実際、面接になると絶対緊張してしまって何も出来ません
dialogue.content: I practice a lot, thinking that I should at least be prepared so my mind doesn't go blank, but when it comes to the actual interview, I always get too nervous and can't do anything.

dialogue.origin: たくさん練習したりして準備をされているのですね、それはとても素晴らしいことですね
dialogue.content: You're preparing by practicing a lot. That's very commendable.

dialogue.origin: でもやっぱり本番は違いますね
dialogue.content: But the real thing is different, after all.

dialogue.origin: そうですよね、緊張感が違いますよね会場に行くまではしっかりと準備されているということですので、
dialogue.content: That's right, the level of tension is different, isn't it. Since you are well-prepared right up until you get to the venue,

dialogue.origin: 本番の前に体をリラックスする方法を少しお伝えさせていただければと思います
dialogue.content: I'd like to share a few ways to relax your body before the actual interview.

dialogue.origin: 緊張すると呼吸が浅くなって体も自然と硬くなってしまいます
dialogue.content: When we're nervous, our breathing becomes shallow and our bodies naturally tense up.

dialogue.origin: そんな方法があるんですか？
dialogue.content: Is there really a way to do that?

dialogue.origin: ええ、もしご興味があれば試してみて下さい実際に私もやっているリラックス法です
dialogue.content: Yes, please try them if you're interested. They're relaxation techniques I use myself.

dialogue.origin: へえー興味があります
dialogue.content: Wow, I'm interested.

dialogue.origin: まずは肩を耳に近づけてぎゅうーっと力を入れてから一気にストンと力を抜くこれを三回やりますまずこれで肩やクビの筋肉の固さが少し和らぐことがあります
dialogue.content: First, bring your shoulders up towards your ears, tense them up tightly, and then suddenly release the tension and let them drop. Do this three times. This can often help ease some of the stiffness in your shoulder and neck muscles.

dialogue.origin: なるほど
dialogue.content: I see.

dialogue.origin: それと呼吸が浅くなると脳にも血流が行きにくくなりますので深呼吸です
dialogue.content: Also, when your breathing becomes shallow, it reduces blood flow to the brain, so deep breathing is very helpful.

dialogue.origin: はい、これなら出来そうです
dialogue.content: Okay, I think I can do that.

dialogue.origin: まず息を吐ききってから4秒かけて吸って4秒かけて吐く次は6秒かけてすって吐く
dialogue.content: First, exhale completely, then inhale for four seconds and exhale for four seconds. Next, try inhaling for six seconds and exhaling for six seconds.

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Okay.

dialogue.origin: これを何回か繰り返すと、体がほぐれるのと同時に今の自分に意識が向きます
dialogue.content: Repeating this a few times will help your body relax and, at the same time, bring your attention to the present moment.

dialogue.origin: そうなんですね。今度の面接のときにやってみます
dialogue.content: I see. I'll try it at my next interview.

dialogue.origin: はい、一度ためしてみてください緊張すると今から面接で失敗したらどうしようとかうまくいかないことをイメージしやすいので体に意識をむけることでマイナスイメージを避ける効果もあるかも知れません
dialogue.content: Yes, please give it a try. When you get nervous, it's easy to imagine things going wrong, like, "What if I fail this interview?" By focusing your attention on your body, you may be able to avoid those negative thoughts.

dialogue.origin: なるほどー！！やってみます！ありがとうございます！！
dialogue.content: I get it! I'll try it! Thank you so much!!

dialogue.origin: 今までたくさんの就活の経験をしたあたなの頑張りはとても価値のある経験ですし素晴らしいと思います準備もしっかりされているので、これからも就活がんばってくださいね
dialogue.content: The effort you've put into your job search so far has been a very valuable experience, and I think that's wonderful. You are also preparing thoroughly, so please continue to do your best.

dialogue.origin: 今日はお話したいことは、話せましたでしょうか？
dialogue.content: Were you able to talk about everything you wanted to today?

dialogue.origin: ありがとうございます！面接受かるように頑張ります！
dialogue.content: Thank you! I'll do my best to pass my interviews!

dialogue.origin: はい、ご健闘をお祈りしていますではまた何かありましたらこちらにご相談にいらして下さいね本日はありがとうございました
dialogue.content: Yes, I'm wishing you the best of luck. If anything else comes up, please feel free to come back and talk with us. Thank you for your time today.

dialogue.origin: また落ち込んだら相談させてください。ありがとうございました
dialogue.content: If I feel down again, I'd like to come back for another session. Thank you very much.

dialogue.origin: はい、おまちしておりますでは、失礼いたします
dialogue.content: Yes, we'll be waiting for you. Goodbye for now.

dialogue.origin: （ありがとうございました）
dialogue.content: (Thank you very much.)

dialogue.origin: (こちらこそありがとうございました相談者役お疲れ様でした後ほど評価を宜しくお願いいたします)
dialogue.content: (Thank you as well. Great job playing the role of the client. Please provide your evaluation later.)

topic.sub: 就職活動の面接緊張問題
